evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 131: sī Juppiter saepe urbēs dēlēvit, frūgēs perdidit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To wipe out completely: a city, an army, a name, a memory. Its first sense is to blot out writing, to erase (Cic. Clu. 41).
Properly to turn upside down, upset (a boat, Cic. de Or. 1.174); then to overthrow a city, a house, a state, a fortune.
To make away with: ruin a person, destroy crops. Its everyday sense is to lose or waste something (operam perdere, to waste one’s effort). Its passive is pereō.

phrases.latin: quae enim domus tam stabilis, quae tam firma cīvitās est, quae nōn odiīs et discidiīs funditus possit ēvertī?
phrases.english: for what house is so stable, what state so firm, that hatred and quarrels could not overturn it from the ground up?
everything was levelled to the ground
